methodology: Identical docking protocol applied to both PDB structures. Receptor shells extracted within 20 Angstrom of relay pocket center. Exhaustiveness 32, 20 modes.

relay_pocket_G465_472.interpretation: Relay pocket residues are atomically identical between 6MEO and 6MET. Same coordinates, same B-factors for all 57 atoms.

control_site_G415_425.interpretation: Control site shows small conformational differences, primarily at Glu424 side chain.

20A_shell.interpretation: Shell has identical atom count and chain composition, but differing atom positions at second-shell residues.

chain_inventory.note: 6MET resolves more of CD4 (chain A), but chain G (gp120) is identical.

analysis.conclusion: The 3.3 kcal/mol cross-structure docking difference is NOT due to pocket wall changes (which are zero) or Vina stochastic variance (which is 0.1 kcal/mol). It arises entirely from second-shell residue packing differences within the 20 Angstrom receptor shell. This demonstrates that rigid-body docking scores are sensitive to conformational context beyond the primary binding site, and motivates the MD ensemble approach for robust druggability assessment.
implications_for_manuscript: Pocket wall (G:465-472) is conformationally invariant across available structures
Docking score variation reflects second-shell breathing, not pocket instability
MD simulations sample this conformational space and provide ensemble-averaged druggability
Strengthens the kinetic window argument: pocket architecture is locked by conservation
